terms.definition: A named position in a lifecycle template, represented as a box in the visual diagram. Phase is the design-time term for what becomes a state at runtime.
An object's recorded condition at runtime. When a document is 'Under Review,' it is in the Under Review state. State is the runtime term for what is called a phase in the template editor.

The boundary between two phases in a lifecycle diagram, represented as a colored vertical bar. Gates are where enforcement happens — workflows can be attached that must complete before an object proceeds.
A named action that moves an object through a gate from one phase to another. Common transitions include Promote, Revise, Lock, and Set State.
The grid in the lifecycle template editor that shows allowed transitions from the currently selected phase. Columns are destination states; rows are transition types.

The foundational permission layer in Windchill. Every object inherits permissions from its administrative domain based on folder and container context. These rules apply regardless of lifecycle state.
An optional permission overlay configured per-state in the lifecycle template editor. Adds permissions that only apply when an object is in a specific state. Cannot revoke domain-level permissions.
A permission grant set directly on an individual object for specific users or groups. The most granular and least scalable permission layer — applies to a single object only.
The fundamental constraint of Windchill access control: permissions can only be granted, never denied. A state-based policy cannot remove a permission that the domain already provides.
Rules that determine what happens when a new object is created — which lifecycle it receives, which team template, default folder, and whether a workflow starts automatically.
A workflow step that tells Windchill to move an object to a specific lifecycle state. References the state by name as text — no cross-validation exists between the workflow and lifecycle template.
A change management configuration that defines which object types can be attached to a change object, whether the attachment is required, and whether it gates lifecycle promotion.
A change management configuration that defines what data flows automatically when one change type creates the next — attributes, associations, and release targets.
A type of mapping rule that copies field values from a source change type to a target change type. Breaks silently if attributes are renamed after configuration.
A type of mapping rule that inherits affected objects (parts, documents) from a source change to a new child change. Off by default in most Windchill installs.
A type of mapping rule that controls when and how associated objects are released with a change event. Configured using Source Value, Mapped Value, and Default fields.
An enforcement mechanism in association rules that blocks lifecycle promotion until a required association exists. Creates a hard process stop, not just a suggestion.
A Windchill change object that captures an identified issue. In a regulatory context, it links to the triggering regulation and initiates the change process.
A change object that plans the response to a Problem Report. Scopes affected parts and documents but may not require them to be finalized.
A change object that implements and releases the change. Requires locked scope (affected parts confirmed) and controls what gets released with the change event.
An internal identifier format used by Windchill for soft types in the OIR table (e.g., wt.doc.WTDocument|8666). Not human-readable — a known gap in OIR usability.
